# #1793: Patch: the deck list marks each card that keeps the deck from being queued
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Sometimes a deck can't be used: it holds a card the player doesn't own enough copies of, a card that was banned or retired, a token, or a custom card. The deck editor lists these problems as sentences above the deck, but the cards themselves look like every other card in the list. After importing a deck code, the player has to hunt for each named card among twenty-five tiles. Once built, each problem card in the deck list carries a warning mark and says what's wrong on hover and to a screen reader, the way a card shared with another deck already does.

## Why
- The validator's per-card errors already name the card: `LoadoutError.cardId` (`crates/engine/src/validator.rs:125`, `apps/web/src/wire/generated/LoadoutError.ts`).
- It is set by the L3, L5 (ownership), L6 and L7 rules (`validator.rs:323-461`).
- `DeckEditor.tsx:300` collects those `errors` and draws them only as text (`DeckEditor.tsx:474-484`, `data-card={issue.cardId}` on a list item).
- `DeckTile` (`DeckSidebar.tsx:96-157`) takes only `conflict`. Its flag, `title` and `aria-label` exist only for a card that is also in another deck.
- The pool side already marks unowned cards (`PoolGrid.tsx:169`, `data-owned`), so the deck side is the odd one out.

## Proposal
- In `DeckEditor`, build a map from card id to the first error naming that card, and pass it to `DeckSidebar`.
- `DeckTile` sets `data-issue={rule}`, adds the error's translated message to its `title` and `aria-label`, and shows the existing `db-tile-flag` mark in a warning tone.
- Errors without a card id stay in the verdict box only.

The client decides nothing new. It shows the verdict the engine's validator already gave (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/DeckEditor.tsx`, `DeckSidebar.tsx`, `deckbuilder.css`
- `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/DeckWorkshop.test.tsx`
- §9.4's loadout rules, read and not changed. No spec change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In a deck with a card the collection owns none of, that card's tile has `data-issue="L5"` and its accessible name includes the error's message.
- [ ] A tile with no error has no `data-issue`.
- [ ] A card that both clashes with another deck and has an error shows both reasons.
- [ ] When the collection couldn't be read, no ownership marks appear, matching the editor's existing hint.
- [ ] Every new string has its `zh-CN.json` entry (`i18n.test.ts`).
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/deckbuilder/DeckWorkshop.test.tsx`, typecheck and eslint pass.

## Size and risks
Small: three files and a test. A tile's accessible name grows for a card in error, so a test that finds tiles by name may need its expected text updated. Test ids stay as they are.
